The 7 live unmapped agents at HEAD d74471a (per the discovery probe) are: coder-kimi-for-coding-highspeed → kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding-highspeed, coder-kimi-for-coding-k2p7 → kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding, coder-openai-gpt-5-6-luna-fast → openai/gpt-5.6-luna-fast, coder-orchestrator → kimi-for-coding/k3, measure-adversarial-testing → deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro, measure-review-a-correctness → kimi-for-coding/kimi-for-coding, measure-ux-browser-review → xiaomi/mimo-v2.5 — all well-formed provider/id shape, so all 7 classify as `map_entry_needed` (not `reference_incorrect`). Zero references are malformed. This is recorded here so Phase 2 Green can produce reconciliation-models.md (or extend metadata.json#deviation_notes) accordingly. The strategy text's stated '3 unmapped' reflects the strategy commit SHA 248d841 state; live state has drifted past the strategy commit due to dirty agent edits adding 4 kimi-using agents. The strategy's reconciliation list (measure-adversarial-testing, measure-ux-browser-review, coder-openai-gpt-5-6-luna-fast) is a strict subset of the live 7.

All openai-codex-based Measure subagents are similarly unavailable: measure-review-a-correctness, measure-review-b-security, measure-review-c-ux-api, measure-phase-acceptance, measure-orchestrator-audit, measure-closeout. Fixtures are static committed files under tests/fixtures/model-resolution/ (not os.tmpdir()-runtime-generated) — chosen for determinism per test-strategy.md §4. Live unmapped count is 7 at HEAD d74471a (not 3 as the strategy text states — the strategy was written at commit SHA 248d841 when the live roster had 3 unmapped agents; the user has since made dirty edits to 4 kimi-using agent files that are present in the working tree but not committed). nonblocking_findings.description: Strategy text states 'Live count at the strategy commit SHA is 3' but live state at HEAD d74471a is 7. The discrepancy is caused by 4 dirty agent edits (coder-kimi-for-coding-highspeed, coder-kimi-for-coding-k2p7, coder-openai-gpt-5-6-luna-fast, coder-orchestrator) that were made after the strategy commit SHA 248d841. The strategy's reconciliation list (measure-adversarial-testing, measure-ux-browser-review, coder-openai-gpt-5-6-luna-fast) is a strict subset of the live 7; the strategy's full 8-name list (which includes the 5 already-mapped names) is reconciled in metadata.json#deviation_notes. Test 7 asserts count >= 3 AND the 7 specific names, so the test is robust to future agent additions and explicitly rejects the false-positive case where unmappedModels === []. Recorded here so Phase 2 Green produces the reconciliation report against live state, not the strategy's frozen list.

Test 5 (suggestion classification) uses parseAgentFile + forced model:undefined to test the suggestion heuristic independently of test 1's passthrough bug. This is intentional because if test 5 relied solely on parseAgentFile's current behavior, it would never reach the suggestion-check assertion (since model === sourceModel for unmapped, the agents would not be classified as unmapped). The forced model:undefined pattern is documented in the test's inline comment. Green will remove the need for this when parseAgentFile returns model:undefined for unmapped (test 1's fix). If Jr Green disagrees with the pattern, they should rewrite test 5 to use the live-roster unmapped agents (which will all be well-formed provider/id after test 1's fix) and assert map_entry_needed for each — but the test would lose the reference_incorrect coverage unless a malformed fixture is added to the live roster itself.

Test 9 (deterministic) includes an existence check (assert.ok(Array.isArray(before.unmappedModelFindings))) before the byte-identical comparison. This is intentional because the field does not yet exist; without the existence check, the test would vacuously pass (both calls return undefined, undefined === undefined). The existence check ensures the test fails at Red with a clear message ('unmappedModelFindings must be an array') and continues to fail if Green lands without the field. This is documented in the test's inline comment.

The Phase 2 model-resolution contract is documented in the JSDoc-style header block of tests/model-resolution.test.mjs (lines 1-72) instead of in lib/core.mjs#parseAgentFile's JSDoc. This is because the absolute constraints prohibit modifying lib/core.mjs in Red. Green (or Phase 2 acceptance) may add the JSDoc to lib/core.mjs#parseAgentFile to mirror the test file's contract surface. The contract content is identical in both locations once Green lands.
